title: What changed in practice

lines: GOOD, OR SILENT. TIE IT, TRUST HIM.
cards: Good, or silent. Tie it, trust Him. Count before you are counted.
The right hand, the name. Plant it anyway. Start next door.
All year the lessons have ended with a short line and one small thing to try. A line like that can be said once and drift off with the day. That's how lines work.
But maybe one didn't. Maybe a bismillah before meals is still there. Maybe a pause before speaking, or a coin set aside each week, or a quick check of the heart before sleep.

teach.h: THE MOST CONSTANT, EVEN IF SMALL.
teach.b: A hadith the year met at the charity jar: in Sahih al-Bukhari, Aisha reports, in paraphrase, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, was asked which deeds are most beloved to Allah, and he said: the most constant of them, even if they are small.
Not the biggest. Not the most dramatic. The ones that keep going.

teach.h: HIS DEEDS WERE LIKE STEADY RAIN.
teach.b: How he lived it: asked whether he set aside special days for extra worship, Aisha answered, in paraphrase, that his deeds were constant, like steady rain, and that none of them could do what he did.
Why small and constant? The year kept circling back to it. The boy at the platter got three short instructions and kept them for life.
The Muwatta's line on character, the hadith on the heart, the tied camel: all practices for an ordinary Tuesday, not a once-a-year push.

teach.h: SMALL ENOUGH TO SURVIVE A BAD DAY.
teach.b: The habits the year asked for were small enough to survive a bad day.
And if nothing stuck? The hadith doesn't ask for a list. It asks for one thing, kept.

And the Qur'an tells those who have wronged themselves, in paraphrase, not to despair of Allah's mercy. Muslims call coming back tawbah, one of the stations the year studied: turning, and beginning again.
So whatever stuck, or didn't, tomorrow's question is the same. What is one small thing, and will it still be there when the day is hard?

how: Muslim teachers encourage small, regular acts over occasional big ones, such as a fixed daily portion of Qur'an, a set extra prayer, or a regular charity, citing the hadith that the most beloved deeds are the most constant, even if small.

games.q: what does “what changed in practice” mean?
o: a new ruling your school issued during the year
the one small habit from the year that kept going
a big change you made once and then let drop

games.q: what changed in practice — tap the pairs.
p: the most constant, even if small

s: Aisha said the Prophet saved his worship for special days
asked that, she said no: his deeds were constant, like steady rain.
the boy at the platter kept his three instructions from then on
in Sahih al-Bukhari, Umar ibn Abi Salamah says that stayed his way of eating.
if no habit stuck, the year was wasted
the Qur'an tells people not to despair of Allah's mercy; tawbah is turning and beginning again.

games.q: a friend says that from tomorrow she'll read the Qur'an for an hour every night, though she hasn't opened it in months. what fits today's hadith?
o: an hour or nothing; small amounts don't count.
start with a few verses a night that she can keep, even on a hard day.
wait for Ramadan and do it all then.
games.why: the most beloved deeds are the most constant, even if small: a few verses kept beat an hour dropped.

practice: Look back over the year for one habit still with you, however small, and be glad of it; if you don't find one, choose one now from the year's lines, small enough to keep.
Picture the exact moment it will happen tomorrow, the kettle, the doorway, the first bite, the last light, and see yourself doing it there.
If a heavier kind of despair comes and stays, please don't carry it alone: in the US, call or text 988, any hour, or elsewhere, local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: What changed in practice. The one habit from the year that kept going, small and constant, the kind the hadith calls most beloved. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the most constant of them, the hadith's word for the deeds most beloved to Allah.

carryVoice: Your line: it stuck. Small and constant, the way steady rain keeps falling. See you tomorrow.
